agent: short reads of the running game, 2026-11-10
question: whether the generator is re-seeded each hour, the order of the hour, and the orders only memory holds

addresses.name: ReseedGlobalRandom
addresses.comment: Re-initialises the global generator from the seed at 0x174DA94 through 0xAA2BF0 with g_random_seed in ecx, zeroes the index, and then **runs the generator forward by g_random_draws draws** - so a generator can be put back where a save left it. Two callers: RunHourlyTick at 0x681C79 and 0x6D7BF2. **It is not run in single-player play**: no hit in 36 hours of a new game, and g_random_draws (0x134DA8C) ran on from 7,771 to 25,530 (read in the running game, 2026-11-10). RunHourlyTick's store of the seed from its payload and its zeroing of the draws (0x681C6B..0x681C79) is a path single-player does not reach; that it is multiplayer's resynchronisation is a reader's and not checked. SnapshotRandomState puts the draws and 0x174DA94 into each hour's payload for it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 1, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: A breakpoint on its entry for 36 hours of a new game, no hit; g_random_draws read at every RunHourlyPass.
addresses.revises: not run in single-player play: the hour does not start a fresh stream

addresses.name: SnapshotRandomState
addresses.comment: Run **every hour** from RunHourlyTick at 0x28207A, on the game state's +0xC58, and ends 0x28250A with a bare `ret`. Clears the vector, then pushes two dwords into it through 0x221F0: g_random_draws (0x174DA8C) and the contents of **0x174DA94**, g_random_init_seed, the figure the generator was made from (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 1). Along the way it lazily allocates a 4-byte object with vftable 0x15FDF60 into 0x174DA90. The same +0xC58 is handed to CHourlyTickCommand::Construct. Named for what it does; no class. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tick.md.
addresses.evidence: ReseedGlobalRandom hands that dword to the initialiser; 86 throughout a new game.

addresses.name: CGameState::RunAIPass
addresses.comment: **The gate that makes the AI hourly.** `ret 4`, one caller: CInGameIdler::Update at 0x656278, so it is offered every frame. Returns at once when `state[+0xC68]` is set; otherwise sets the global byte 0x1A857BF, launches the ProcessAI parallel_for (0x28E430) over `state[+0x114..+0x118]` with grain `max(1, count / ([0x170ABB0] == 1 ? 1 : 16))`, restores the global and sets `state[+0xC68] = 1`. **RunHourlyPass clears +0xC68 at its end (0x682B1D)**, and a byte-exact sweep finds no other clear, so the AI runs exactly once per game hour. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ai.md. **So the AI runs after every pass of the hour, the daily pass included**, and its 102 countries in a different order each hour on the workers; what they post runs after all of them, before the next tick (seen in the running game, 2026-11-10; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 2).
addresses.evidence: Breakpoints on RunHourlyPass, ProcessAI and CommandExecute_CallSite for 36 hours: HOUR, then 102 AI, then EXEC, every hour.

addresses.name: g_random_init_seed
addresses.comment: The figure the game's generator was made from: ReseedGlobalRandom passes it to the initialiser (0xAA2BF0) with the state array at 0x1310F80 in ecx. 86 throughout a new game in the running game. SnapshotRandomState puts it into each hour's tick payload beside g_random_draws.
addresses.evidence: ReseedGlobalRandom at VA 0xAA2F04: mov eax,[0x174DA94]; mov ecx,0x1620F80 in the live base; call of the initialiser.

struct_fields.name: OwnedProvinces
struct_fields.comment: The game's own name for it, out of the Lua API. `CCountry::GetOwnedProvinces` (rva 0x3A660) is `lea eax, [ecx + 0xcf0]; ret` - the whole function, so the function *is* the offset. The first of the three province CLists - owned at +0xCF0, controlled at +0xD00, core at +0xD10, each 0x10 bytes with its count at +8. CAnyOwnedProvinceTrigger::Evaluate walks this one. In province-number order on a new game (read in the running game, 2026-11-10).
struct_fields.evidence: 76 of 76 countries of two or more

struct_fields.name: ControlledProvinces
struct_fields.comment:
the head of a list of `{ province id, ?, next }` nodes - CCountry::UpdateIC walks it and looks each id up in CCurrentGameState +0xB8C to sum the country's IC. **It is the controlled provinces**, settled by the game's own Lua accessor `CCountry::GetControlledProvinces` (VA 0x417AE0 = `lea eax,[ecx+0xD00]; ret`), with `NumberOfControlledProvinces` the CList's own count member at +0xD08 (`CCountry::GetNumberOfControlledProvinces`, VA 0x5010C0). The pair for the owned provinces is +0xCF0 / +0xCF8, which CAnyOwnedProvinceTrigger::Evaluate walks and CCountry::RebuildNeighbours's first province walk uses. The earlier inference from the +0x610 test was right.

**Renamed from `province_ids` and retyped 2026-10-05.** The comment already said the game's own accessor settles it; the name and type now say so too. `lea eax,[ecx+0xD00]` at rva 0x17AE0 is registered as `CList<int> const& CCountry::GetControlledProvinces()`, so the field is the whole embedded CList - `first` at +0xD00, `last` at +0xD04, `count` at +0xD08 (which is what `CCountry::GetNumberOfControlledProvinces`, rva 0x1010C0, returns) and the node byte at +0xD0C. In province-number order on a new game (read in the running game, 2026-11-10).
struct_fields.evidence: 76 of 76 countries of two or more

struct_fields.name: CoreProvinces
struct_fields.comment:
The head of a linked list of province ids the country claims, each node's next at +0x8. The alignment revanchism term walks it and counts the provinces whose current owner belongs to the faction being scored. **The game's own name for it is `CoreProvinces`**, from the Lua accessor `CCountry::GetCoreProvinces` (VA 0x4C3040 = `lea eax,[ecx+0xD10]; ret`, registered returning `CList<int>&`) - so these are HoI3's core provinces, the country side of the per-province `cores` list at `CProvince +0x344` that the event language's `is_core` and `any_core` triggers walk.

**Renamed from `claims` and retyped 2026-10-05**, on the authority the comment already cited: `lea eax,[ecx+0xD10]` at rva 0xC3040, registered as `CList<int> const& CCountry::GetCoreProvinces()`. `claims` is EU3's word; HoI3 calls these core provinces, and conflating the two is a real risk because HoI3 also has claims in the peace machinery. In province-number order on a new game (read in the running game, 2026-11-10).
struct_fields.evidence: 90 of 90 countries of two or more
